thesis: Palermo in October is the month the city stops hosting and gets itself back.
scene: It's 7pm in the Vucciria. The last tourist has walked back to the hotel. The fruit vendor is packing up the day's last mangoes and giving two of them to a woman who did not ask and does not seem surprised. A group of teenagers on scooters circles the fountain, going nowhere, twice. A man is setting up a table on the pavement outside his building that has no stated purpose but will be there until midnight, and by nine there will be four chairs at it. The shutters that were closed all afternoon are open. Nobody is taking photos.

sceneAnchors.text: The oldest market in Palermo where October means the vendors are selling to the neighborhood again. Eggplants the size of a fist. Someone arguing the price of swordfish. The market that does not adjust itself for visitors.

The baroque fountain the locals call the piazza of shame. In October, after 9pm, it belongs to couples, old men in chairs, teenagers on the steps. The tour groups have gone and the lighting that was built for photographs is now lighting for sitting under.

The beach town fifteen minutes from the center that is abandoned by September and reclaimed in October by Palermitani who go there on a Tuesday because they can. The lido chairs are mostly stacked. The water is still warm.

locals: Going to Mondello on a weekday, because the bus is not full and the chairs are stacked and the water is still warm. Shopping at Ballaro without a list, and being handed things by vendors who have decided what you are having. Sitting in the piazza without acknowledging that it is a famous piazza. Eating arancine at the bar on the corner for breakfast because that is what you do on a Tuesday in October. The evening passeggiata restarts at an hour that would have been unbearable in August.

localWord.translation: to take a walk that is not for exercise or destination
localWord.body: The Italian institution, but October in Palermo is when it reclaims its original meaning. The passeggiata is not tourism. It is being in the city without a reason. In October you do not need one.

changes: The street noise changes register. The summer sound — scooter horns, raised voices, tourists with maps — softens into the October sound, which is the city talking to itself. You start to hear it around day two. After that you notice that nobody is speaking English at you, and that the volume has not dropped, only changed audience.
start: Walking without the map, and being wrong about where you are for twenty minutes without it costing anything. Eating at the counter, standing, at the hour the people beside you are eating. Going to the market before the bread runs out, which is earlier than you think and is not posted anywhere. You start taking the long way through the piazza in the evening because everyone else is.
stop: The itinerary. Palermo in October does not reward the plan; it rewards the detour, and the detour is usually a street that looked closed and was not. You stop deciding where dinner is before seven. The city has more opinions about your evening than you do, and October is when it is willing to share them.
returns: The sense that you are in someone else's city, not a set for your photos. That the square you are standing in existed before you arrived and will exist after you leave.
remember: The summer left and took the audience with it. You stayed.

items.label: August
items.body: The city runs at full tourist capacity and the locals go to the mountains.

items.label: October
items.body: Ballaro opens at 6am and only Palermitani are there.

items.label: December
items.body: The city goes quiet for a different reason and the streets belong to those who never left.
